hub.name: Fractions, one piece at a time

questions.explanation: Three of six equal parts cover half of the whole.

questions.prompt: To turn 2/3 into sixths, what do you do?
questions.explanation: Each third splits into two sixths, giving four sixths.

questions.prompt: What happens to the value when 6/8 is simplified to 3/4?
questions.explanation: Both numbers were divided by two, so the amount is unchanged.

title: Why 1/2 and 2/4 mean the same amount
practice: Try a few problems at your own pace, then return to any explanation you want to revisit.

sections.html:
Fold a paper strip in half and shade one half. Fold it again so the whole strip has four equal sections. The shaded area now covers two sections.

You can describe that same area as 1/2 or 2/4. These are equivalent fractions: different written fractions with the same value. Folding did not add or remove any shaded paper.
sections.title: A second fold changes the labels

sections.html:
Draw two identical strips and shade half of each. Leave the first in two equal parts. Divide the second into six equal parts, keeping its shaded area unchanged.

Each original half becomes three smaller pieces. There are six pieces in the whole and three selected pieces: 1/2 = 3/6. Both strips cover exactly the same length.
sections.title: Try it yourself

sections.html:
Draw a strip with three equal pieces and colour two of them. You have coloured 2/3 of the strip.

  1. Cut each of the three pieces in half.
  2. The strip now has six equal pieces altogether.
  3. The coloured part now covers four of those pieces.

The same coloured amount is now called 4/6. That is why 2/3 and 4/6 are equivalent fractions: they name the same share of the same whole.

Both numbers doubled because every piece was split in two. The amount of colour stayed the same.
sections.title: Smaller pieces, same amount

sections.html:
You can also join small pieces together. Draw eight equal pieces and colour six. That shows 6/8.

  1. Put the eight pieces into pairs. There are four pairs.
  2. The six coloured pieces make three coloured pairs.
  3. Three of the four pairs are coloured, so the same amount is 3/4.

Writing a fraction with smaller numbers like this is called simplifying. You have not made the share smaller; you have given it a simpler name.

In the same way, four of eight pieces cover half the strip. So 4/8 and 1/2 name the same amount.
sections.title: Join pieces back together

description: Split each piece again and watch the numbers change while the shaded amount stays still.
